name: Utah
overview: Utah counties sell real property with delinquent taxes at an annual tax sale that the county auditor conducts in May or June. A property is offered once its period of redemption is expiring, which comes after the lapse of four years from the date the taxes became delinquent. Until then, anyone may redeem the property on behalf of the record owner at any time before the tax sale. Each county sets its own date, format and payment rules within that window.

counties.how_to_bid: The sale runs on the Public Surplus online auction site. Bidding starts at the total of taxes, interest, penalties and administrative costs owed on the parcel. counties.how_to_bid: Register in person on sale day (pre-registration starts at 9:00 am) with a government-issued photo ID to receive a bidder number. Bidding is open auction to the highest bidder; the opening bid includes taxes, penalties, interest and cost of sale. The Treasurer's Department collects the successful bid and recording fee immediately after the auction closes; the FAQ lists cash, business checks or personal checks and says no financing is offered.

counties.next_sale_note: 2027 date not yet posted. The county page still shows the 2026 sale, which began Thursday, May 28, 2026 at 10:00 AM online on Public Surplus (past).
counties.how_to_bid: Online only, through Public Surplus; register there. For the 2026 sale a refundable credit card deposit was charged at your first bid on each property ($50 for properties with a tax value of $10,000 or less, $100 above that); the deposit is not applied to the price. Winning bidders received emailed instructions and paid in full by wire transfer through Public Surplus within 5 business days; tax deeds are recorded and mailed in about 4 to 6 weeks. Property can be redeemed until the sale starts. The county advises calling the office to confirm wire details before sending money.
